newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares slip on thin volume, skimpy buying.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares slip on thin volume, skimpy buying.

text.p: Leading Russian shares slipped on Monday in a market supported by Russian buying and small Western orders, traders said.
The Russian Trading System RTS index of 23 shares fell by 2.32 percent to 322.31 on $24.79 million in total volume.
"If it were not for Russian money, support prices could have fallen about five percent," said IK Aton trader Alexander Bobolev.

"The fact that Russian participation in the market has widened cannot be neglected. Although the participants who are selling now are stronger than our buyers, one cannot help taking our support into consideration."
United City Bank chief trader Samit Yakovlev forecast no substantial rise in the market in the near future.
"The market has become very selective -- all paper will not rise at the same time any longer," he said.
"Even in the second-tier shares, people are taking a cautious approach. I think they will now look at companies' annual results."
He said the best Western demand was for oil company Surgutneftegaz ordinary shares and Rostelekom telecom shares.
Surgutneftegaz ordinary stock rose to $0.833 from $0.824 at Friday's close and Rostelekom edged up to $4.00 from $3.93.
Norilsk Nickel metals group fell to $6.70 from $6.92 following news that the company's trade union was preparing a strike over unpaid salaries and vacation packages.
